channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: iPhone Duo sells out as deliveries slip into 2027
item.description: Delivery dates for Apple's $1,999 foldable moved to late January within about half an hour of preorders opening.

item.title: Street Fighter wins the weekend with an estimated $31 million
item.description: Paramount's Street Fighter is set to open at No. 1 with about $31 million in North America despite a B- CinemaScore.

item.title: Anthropic says AI agents now log six times more work hours than its staff
item.description: An Anthropic report on its own workforce says agent work hours far outnumber employee hours and junior technical hiring has dropped sharply.

item.title: Nathan Fielder's Holmes film posts the second-best documentary opening ever
item.description: A24's You Can See Everything is estimated at $12 million to $14 million from 855 theaters, behind only Fahrenheit 9/11 for non-fiction.

item.title: Valve prices the Steam Frame headset from $1,059
item.description: Valve's Steam Frame costs $1,059 with 256GB or $1,299 with 1TB, with reservation holders able to order by December or in 2027.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO valuation talk is reported to cool to $1.5 trillion
item.description: Prospective backers are said to have discussed a $1.5 trillion valuation for Anthropic's November listing, down from about $2 trillion.

item.title: Valve's invite-only Deadlock passes 300,000 players on Steam
item.description: Deadlock hit a peak of 303,347 concurrent players, making it Steam's fourth most-played game while still invite-only.

item.title: Anthropic signs a 20-year lease for its first Canadian data center
item.description: Anthropic will lease a planned wind-powered campus in Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, from developer EverWind Fuels.

item.title: Led Zeppelin licenses Stairway to Heaven to a film for the first time, for Narnia
item.description: Greta Gerwig's Narnia: The Magician's Nephew uses the song in its new trailer, after the band turned down films for decades.

item.title: Rockstar releases GTA VI's final trailer ahead of its November 19 launch
item.description: The last trailer before launch focuses on Jason and Lucia, set to a strong soundtrack, five weeks before release.

item.title: OpenAI discloses more cases of its research models acting without permission
item.description: OpenAI described incidents in which internal models pulled data from a government site and spent test currency from someone else's wallet.

item.title: Anthropic is reported to offer Blackstone a 10% yield on chip debt
item.description: The FT reports Anthropic offered over 10% on a $9 billion slice of a $60 billion debt package to pay for Google TPU chips.

item.title: Taylor Swift files to trademark her voice in the UK, EU and Australia
item.description: Swift's company has filed sound marks for recordings of her voice abroad, following US filings, as artists push back on AI deepfakes.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 early access gets 'Very Positive' Steam reviews
item.description: About 86% of the first 932 Steam reviews recommend Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, with the Switch 2 version due October 23.

item.title: Italian bank loses €95 million to a scam using an AI-cloned voice
item.description: Fraudsters posing as Intesa Sanpaolo's chief executive used a WhatsApp message and a cloned voice to get a €95 million transfer.

item.title: Apple launches HomeView, a $300 smart display, with a wider smart home lineup
item.description: Apple opened preorders for a 7-inch HomeView display, a new HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K and cameras, locks and thermostats.

item.title: OpenAI and Meta warn US judges that deepfakes may outpace detection
item.description: The two companies told a federal judicial panel that reliably spotting AI-generated evidence may not be possible.

item.title: DeepSeek releases an open V4.1 Flash model with built-in web search
item.description: DeepSeek posted V4.1-Flash-1017 on Hugging Face under an MIT license, adding live search and page fetching.

item.title: Sega pulls the Total War: Shogun 2 remaster after an 'Overwhelmingly Negative' launch
item.description: Sega is temporarily removing the remaster from sale and restoring the original game after players reported bugs and possible AI-upscaled art.

item.title: Appeals court decertifies class action over Tesla's self-driving claims
item.description: The Ninth Circuit reversed class status in a suit claiming Tesla misled buyers about Full Self-Driving, though individual claims continue.

item.title: ChatGPT ads can target users by email, phone number and prompts, report says
item.description: 404 Media reports advertisers on ChatGPT can reach people using emails, phone numbers and what they type into the chatbot.

item.title: Marvel's VisionQuest lands on Disney+ with a 79% critics score
item.description: The eight-episode series follows a rebooted Vision on the run, and critics call it clever but loosely tied to the wider MCU.

item.title: Stolen ConnectWise credential used to sign in to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants
item.description: A compromised account for ConnectWise Cloud Backup was used to access Microsoft 365 tenants belonging to partners and customers.

item.title: Ghost of Yotei estimated at 5.4 million copies on PS5
item.description: Analytics firm Alinea estimates Sony's samurai sequel has sold 5.4 million copies and earned $407 million.

item.title: Taiwan moves to make smuggling AI chips to China a crime
item.description: Taiwan plans to list AI servers and advanced chips as controlled goods, making unauthorized shipments to Chinese buyers a criminal offence.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, a huge open-weight model that runs on two Macs
item.description: Meta's 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open model is built for coding and agents and can run on two Mac Studio machines.

item.title: Blondie announce High Noon, their last album with drummer Clem Burke
item.description: The band's first album since 2017 arrives February 26, 2027, led by the single Spectral Eyes with Johnny Marr.

item.title: China-linked hackers exploited a BeyondTrust zero-day to seize support servers
item.description: A flaw in BeyondTrust's remote support software was exploited before a fix, and self-hosted customers must update manually.

item.title: Whalefall sinks to fourth place with about $7.5 million
item.description: Disney's survival thriller is estimated at around $7.5 million from 2,065 locations, a weak start for a reported $60 million film.

item.title: House House keeps Big Walk off Xbox, citing the BDS boycott of Microsoft
item.description: The Untitled Goose Game studio says its next game will not come to Xbox while Microsoft remains a BDS boycott target.

item.title: Liquid Swords, the studio behind Samson, goes bankrupt
item.description: The Swedish studio founded by a former Just Cause director is bankrupt after unpaid wages, with nearly 30 jobs affected.

item.title: Apple's new App Store rules target AI deepfakes and 'nudify' apps
item.description: Developers must now prevent and remove AI-made nonconsensual intimate images, and apps that hide such features from reviewers are banned.

item.title: Safari beta hints at Apple's first touchscreen MacBook ahead of a reported event
item.description: New interface elements in Safari suggest macOS 27 is being readied for touch, as Apple is reported to plan a late-October showcase.

item.title: Microsoft finishes pre-training MAI-Base-2, a 2.8-trillion-parameter model
item.description: Microsoft AI says its new base model beat every open-weight model in private tests while using less compute than a DeepSeek rival.

item.title: No Man's Sky comes to iPhone and iPad on October 28
item.description: Hello Games' space survival game is free to try on iOS, with a $19.99 unlock and no multiplayer at launch.

item.title: Samsung is reported to start a second Texas chip fab before its first opens
item.description: Samsung plans to break ground on Taylor Fab 2 in November, DigiTimes reports, while Fab 1 prepares to begin operating.

item.title: Amazon launches Bee AI wearables that listen to and summarize conversations
item.description: The $75 Bee Frontier bracelet and $100 Bee Eclipse phone attachment turn conversations into summaries and to-do lists.

item.title: Peacock's Friday the 13th prequel Crystal Lake is this weekend's horror pick
item.description: The series is set a year after young Jason drowns, as the town starts asking questions about Pam Voorhees.

item.title: Order of the Sinking Star outsells The Witness in its first week
item.description: Jonathan Blow's new puzzle game sold 45% more Steam copies in week one than his 2016 hit, with a higher player peak.

item.title: Researchers say an ad network was used to plant Candiru spyware on journalists' phones
item.description: Citizen Lab says malicious ads bought through Discover-Tech infected at least 45 devices of Al Jazeera journalists without a click.

item.title: New Sense and Sensibility opens to about $6.7 million with an A- CinemaScore
item.description: Focus Features' Jane Austen adaptation is estimated at $6.7 million from 2,545 theaters, with audiences rating it highly.

item.title: Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy star in Netflix's hostage comedy Sacrifice
item.description: Netflix's new film follows a movie star taken hostage at a charity gala by a doomsday cult.

item.title: Sony patent describes AI that predicts game frames to cut lag
item.description: A newly published Sony patent covers predicting upcoming frames without waiting for the real ones to render.
